messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Japanese, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Japanese line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
彼は彼女をすべての町で追い回すだろう、 彼が彼女を地獄に戻すまでだろう、 そこは嫉妬が最初に彼女を送り出した場所だ。

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Japanese Mapping Table**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Word/Phrase | Back‑Translation | Status | |-------------|----------------------|--------------------|-------------------|--------| | Questi | male agent who will hunt | 彼は | “he” (subject) | OK | | la | female patient of the hunt | 彼女を | “her” (object) | OK | | caccerà | future “shall hunt” | 追い回すだろう | “shall hunt” | OK | | per | preposition “through” (locative) | で | particle marking location | OK | | ogne | quantifier “every” | すべての | “every” | OK | | villa | “town” (location) | 町 | “town” | OK | | fin | conjunction “until” (temporal limit) | までだろう | “until …” | OK | | che | complementizer “that” (introduces clause) | — | — | **UNNECESSARY** (Japanese does not use an explicit word) | | l'avrà | auxiliary “shall have” (future perfect) | — | — | **UNNECESSARY** (encoded in the “までだろう” construction) | | rimessa | verb “set back” | 戻す | “return / set back” | OK | | ne | preposition “in” (locative) | に | “to / in” | OK | | lo | definite article “the” (masc.) | — | — | **UNNECESSARY** (articles are omitted in Japanese) | | 'nferno | “hell” (destination) | 地獄 | “hell” | OK | | là | adverb of place “there” | そこは | “there (as a topic)” | OK | | onde | relative adverb “whence” (introduces causal clause) | — | — | **UNNECESSARY** (covered by そこは) | | 'nvidia | personified “envy” (cause) | 嫉妬 | “envy” | OK | | prima | temporal adverb “first” | 最初に | “first (time)” | OK | | dipartilla | verb “shall send forth” (future) | 送り出した | “sent forth” (past‑relative form) | OK |
---
### Items Requiring Attention - **UNNECESSARY**: `che`, `l'avrà`, `lo`, `onde` – Japanese does not require explicit equivalents for these functional words; their meanings are absorbed by the surrounding grammar or omitted naturally. - **MISSING / WRONG / GRAMMAR**: none.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Japanese script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Japanese text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).

- Line 1: - Original: 彼は彼女をすべての町で追い回すだろう、 - Issue: none - Corrected: no change
- Line 2: - Original: 彼が彼女を地獄に戻すまでだろう、 - Issue: none - Corrected: no change
- Line 3: - Original: そこは嫉妬が最初に彼女を送り出した場所だ。 - Issue: none - Corrected: no change
